holidays.name: Clean Out Your Refrigerator Day
holidays.description: Time to face the fuzzy science experiments lurking behind the pickle jars. Today you toss the mystery leftovers, expired condiments and that suspicious container nobody dares to open, then wipe down the shelves until the fridge sparkles.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is often linked to the pre-Thanksgiving timing, since a clean fridge makes room for holiday feasts.
holidays.funFact: Condiments tend to outlast everything else in the fridge. Many households keep bottles of sauce well past their prime, so the door shelves are often the best place to start.

holidays.name: Little Red Wagon Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the classic children's toy that has hauled toys, pets, siblings and the occasional bag of groceries. Pull out a wagon and take a nostalgic ride.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that honors the iconic red wagon, a symbol of American childhood. The toy traces back to Antonio Pasin, an Italian immigrant who founded Radio Flyer in Chicago.
holidays.funFact: Radio Flyer's name reflects its founder's fascination with two marvels of his era: the radio and flight. Pasin started out building wooden wagons by hand.

holidays.name: I Love to Write Day
holidays.description: A day for anyone who loves putting words on paper. Poets, novelists, journal keepers and napkin doodlers are all invited to pick up a pen and write something.
holidays.origin: Created by author John Riddle in 2002 to encourage writing and reading. It grew into a national observance, and it is celebrated on the same date each year.
holidays.funFact: The day was started to promote the joy of writing, and it is often celebrated with writing contests and events in schools and libraries.
